chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

the one in Ihram who has intercourse with his wife: He (peace be upon him) said: If he has fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and Hajj the following year; and if he has not fully entered into her, then upon him is a camel, and there is not upon him Hajj the following year.

He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about a man who had intercourse with his wife while he was in Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: If he was ignorant, then there is nothing upon him; and if he was not ignorant, then upon him is the driving of a camel, and upon him is Hajj the following year.

So when he reaches the place where he had intercourse with her, their two caravans are separated, so they do not gather in one tent unless there is someone else with them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its place.

key_terms.أَفْضَى إِلَيْهَا: He fully entered into her (consummated the act)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.يَقَعُ عَلَى أَهْلِهِ: He has intercourse with his wife

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific expiations (kaffarah) for sexual intercourse during Hajj Ihram, distinguishing liability based on full penetration versus partial contact and the state of ignorance (jahil) versus knowledge. It further elaborates on the practical ritual of separating the sacrificial animal from the pilgrim's baggage until it reaches its designated slaughter site, reflecting the juristic precision of the Imams in regulating the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the one in Ihraam falling upon his wife. Heasws said: ‘If he has gone into her, so upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and he (performing of the) Hajj the next year. And if he had not gone into her, so upon him would be a sacrificial animal, and there would not be a Hajj upon him the next year’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I asked himasws about a man who falls upon his wife, and he is in Ihraam. Heasws said: ‘If he was ignorant, so there is nothing upon him; and if he did not happen to be ignorant, so upon him would be ushering of a sacrificial animal, and upon him would be the Hajj next year.

So when he ends up to the place where he fell upon her, separation would be effect between their two carriages, so they would not be gathered in one tent unless there happens to be someone else along with the two of them, until the sacrificial animal reaches its place’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “About a man who is in the state of Ihram and performs sexual relation with his wife, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If intercourse has taken place, he owes a badanah and al-Hajj in future; if it has not taken place, he owes one badanah but not al-Hajj in future.’

I then asked, about a man who performs sexual relation with his wife while he is in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he does not know the rule he does not owe anything. If he is not ignorant, then he must drive a badanah and he owes al-Hajj in future.

When he arrives at the place where it had happened they must separate from each other’s carriage and must not sit together in one tent unless there is a third person present with them until the offering reaches its place.’”
